item_verdicts.evidence: Strong and largely independently reproducible: the grep-clean claim was re-run here on the copy (no hits for any of the eleven deleted names); the per-row token/cost comparison was reproduced arithmetically from watch-read.json for all four periods; the negative control is real and disagrees (the mutated copy prints 128M for the 1-hour row against the document's 90.9M, EXIT=0, negative-control.txt); the capture shows the four period rows, the serve card rows, the mean row and the job-table header. Held below full for two gaps. (1) The boundary-state claims in compare.md (STALE at published_at 1000 s, MISSING, UNPARSABLE) are implemented in the copy (the _watch_document function prints 'watch document unavailable'/'unparsable'/'stale <age>'), but the run they came from used a /tmp scratch (gwstates-3rt2vo29) that no durable log retains, so a reader can read the claims but cannot re-run them. (2) The eight-card-row requirement is unmet and only partially evidenced (four rows shown, honestly disclosed).
item_verdicts.fit: Fits the section's design cleanly: gpu-watch stays a standalone script and consumes the published JSON document rather than importing the package, so the document is the single contract; the period ledger and its ledger and cost column come from that document, the serve panel's lane/live blocks come from `agent watch --json --live`, and the node half (card bars, node job table, host load, live mode) is untouched. Two observations, neither blocking: the copy still reaches the engine over HTTP for pre-existing non-ledger paths - _scrape_serve/vllm_load as a fallback when no overlappable step supplies card readings (copy lines 1126, 1527) and _serve_state_tail's /v1/models probe for the serve card's context window (line 494) - which the section's prose ('no serving figure is computed in the dotfiles repository') arguably also covers, though the dispatch's explicit deletion list did not name them and §11 governs the live panel; and the four-of-eight card rows is a state-of-the-node limitation that a login-node run would render as eight.
